facts.value: Comparative religion is the branch of the study of religions concerned with the systematic comparison of the doctrines and practices of the world's religions.
The comparative study of religion yields a deeper understanding of the fundamental philosophical concerns of religion such as ethics, metaphysics, and the nature and form of salvation.
Studying such material is meant to give one a richer and more sophisticated understanding of human beliefs and practices regarding the sacred, numinous, spiritual, and divine.

A common geographical classification of the main world religions includes Middle Eastern religions, Indian religions, East Asian religions, African religions, American religions, Oceanic religions, and classical Hellenistic religions.
